I/O context structure for the GD library. Holds function pointers implementing read/write/seek/tell and an optional destructor (gd_free), plus a user data pointer. Used by GD image read/write APIs to abstract file/stream operations. getC/getBuf are required for reading; putC/putBuf for writing; seek/tell are needed for gd2 random access. gd_free, if provided, should release any resources associated with the context. The concrete behavior depends on the function pointers supplied.

objects.definition: typedef int (*gdCacheTestFn_t)(void *userdata, void *keydata);
objects.description: Pointer-to-function type used by the cache to test whether a cached userdata matches provided keydata. Returns nonzero on match. Ownership/lifetime of userdata is managed by the cache; keydata is provided by the caller.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*gdCacheFetchFn_t)(char **error, void *keydata);
objects.description: Pointer-to-function type used by the cache to construct/fetch a userdata object on cache miss. Returns a newly created userdata pointer or NULL on failure. May set *error to a descriptive message string managed by the callee or caller (unspecified by this header).

objects.definition: typedef void (*gdCacheReleaseFn_t)(void *userdata);
objects.description: Pointer-to-function type used by the cache to release/destroy a userdata object when evicted or when the cache is deleted. Must correctly free any resources owned by userdata.
Singly linked list node representing one cached entry. Holds a pointer to the user-managed payload (userdata) and a link to the next element in LRU order.

Cache head/handle for an LRU cache of userdata pointers. Tracks the most-recently-used list head, current size, last error string, and the user-supplied callbacks for test, fetch (on miss), and release. Create with gdCacheCreate; delete with gdCacheDelete. Not thread-safe unless externally synchronized.

RGBA color holder for libgd. Internally stores either packed int or per-channel bytes (BGRA order in inner struct). Provides getters/setters and conversion to int color values used by libgd.

C++ RAII wrapper around libgd gdImagePtr. Owns the gdImagePtr and destroys it in the destructor. Provides constructors for new images, from streams, FILE*, memory, and tag-dispatched format-specific loaders (PNG, GIF, WBMP, JPEG, GD, GD2, XBM). Exposes a rich set of drawing, color, copying, scaling, rotation, text, and encoding methods that forward to libgd. Copy makes a deep image copy. Clone/Scale/RotateInterpolated/CopyGaussianBlurred allocate new Image instances that the caller must delete.

Pointer type to a gd font structure used by the GD graphics library. This header only references this type and does not define it; its full definition resides in gd.h. Used here to expose the Giant built-in font instance and an accessor.

functions.name: gdAlphaBlend
functions.description: Composites two truecolor ARGB pixels using the source alpha; returns an opaque blended color. Intended for internal and caller-side color compositing.
requirements: dest and src must be 32-bit truecolor values with 7-bit alpha in the most significant 7 bits (0..127).
Alpha range is 0 (opaque) to 127 (transparent).
Not intended for palette indices.

functions.name: gdLayerOverlay
functions.description: Applies an overlay layer-blend between two truecolor pixels and returns resulting opaque color.
requirements: dest and src must be 32-bit truecolor ARGB values (alpha 0..127).
Behavior applies to truecolor pixels; not palette indices.

functions.name: gdLayerMultiply
functions.description: Applies multiply blend mode between two truecolor pixels; returns resulting opaque color.
requirements: dest and src must be 32-bit truecolor ARGB values (alpha 0..127).
For truecolor use only.

functions.name: gdSetErrorMethod
functions.description: Installs a global error reporting callback (printf-like) for GD operations.
requirements: callback must be a function of type void (*)(int, const char *, va_list).
Must be called before operations to receive errors.
Thread-safety of global callback is unspecified; set before multithreaded use.

functions.name: gdClearErrorMethod
functions.description: Clears any previously installed error reporting callback.
requirements: Call to restore default error handling.
Affects process-global handler.

functions.name: gdImageCreate
functions.description: Creates a palette-based image of given width and height (up to 256 colors).

functions.name: gdImageSetPixel

requirements: im must be valid.

functions.name: gdImageStringTTF

functions.description: Deprecated wrapper that calls gdImageStringFT. Returns NULL on success, or error string on failure.
requirements: If im is not NULL, draws text on image using fg color; if im is NULL, computes bounding box only (common GD pattern).
brect (int[8]) may receive bounding box; must point to 8-int buffer if non-NULL.

Caller must free returned error string? (Unknown; per GD, returned char* is static or allocated—documentation suggests error string ownership unknown).

functions.name: gdImageStringFT
functions.signature: char * gdImageStringFT(gdImagePtr im, int *brect, int fg, const char *fontlist, double ptsize, double angle, int x, int y, const char *string);
functions.description: Renders text via FreeType. Returns NULL on success, or a malloc'ed error string on failure.
requirements: FreeType must be available.
If im is NULL, computes bounding box only; otherwise draws on image.
brect should be an array of 8 ints to receive bounding box if non-NULL.
fontlist must be valid (path(s) or fontconfig pattern depending on gdFTUseFontConfig).
Caller must gdFree the returned non-NULL error string (per comment of gdFTStringExtra xshow/fontpath; general GD docs state error string is malloc'ed).

functions.name: gdFTUseFontConfig
functions.description: Configures whether fontconfig patterns are used for font selection. Returns 0 if fontconfig not available, nonzero otherwise.
requirements: Call before gdImageStringFT/Ex when using fontconfig patterns.

functions.name: gdImageStringFTEx
functions.signature: char * gdImageStringFTEx(gdImagePtr im, int *brect, int fg, const char *fontlist, double ptsize, double angle, int x, int y, const char *string, gdFTStringExtraPtr strex);
functions.description: Extended FreeType text rendering with extra parameters (kerning, DPI, charmap, etc.). Returns NULL on success, or a malloc'ed error string on failure.
requirements: FreeType must be available.
strex may be NULL or point to a gdFTStringExtra struct with flags/options set.
If strex->flags includes gdFTEX_XSHOW or gdFTEX_RETURNFONTPATHNAME, caller must gdFree the returned xshow/fontpath strings.
If im is NULL, computes bounding box only; otherwise draws on image.

functions.name: gdPutC
functions.signature: void gdPutC(const unsigned char c, gdIOCtxPtr ctx);
functions.description: Writes a single byte to the output associated with the given gdIOCtx (via ctx->putC). Use when emitting image data to a custom IO context. Endianness is not applicable for single-byte writes. Errors are not reported via return value; the context may track failures internally.
requirements: ctx must be non-null.
ctx must point to an initialized gdIOCtx suitable for writing.
ctx->putC must be non-null and valid.
c should be a byte value in the range 0..255 (unsigned char).
Caller cannot detect write failure from this function’s return (it returns void); if needed, use a context that tracks error state.

functions.name: gdPutBuf
functions.signature: int gdPutBuf(const void *buf, int size, gdIOCtxPtr ctx);
functions.description: Writes size bytes from buf to the output associated with ctx (via ctx->putBuf). Returns the number of bytes actually written; a value less than size indicates an error/short write.
requirements: ctx must be non-null.
ctx must point to an initialized gdIOCtx suitable for writing.
ctx->putBuf must be non-null and valid.
If size > 0, buf must be non-null and point to at least size bytes readable memory.
size must be non-negative.
Caller must check the return value and handle short writes or errors.

functions.name: gdPutWord
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit word to ctx. By convention in gd, this is big-endian (most-significant byte first); a separate LSB variant exists for little-endian reads. Used for serializing 16-bit values in gd file formats. Exact endianness is inferred from naming; documentation does not state it explicitly here.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for writing.
ctx->putC and/or ctx->putBuf must be available to perform the write.
w should be in the range 0..65535; values outside this range will be truncated to 16 bits (behavior implied by writing a 16-bit quantity).
Function returns void; caller cannot detect failures except via context-specific mechanisms.

functions.name: gdPutInt
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit integer to ctx. In gd this is typically big-endian (MSB first); little-endian read helpers exist separately. Used for serializing 32-bit values. Exact endianness and integer width assumptions are inferred and not explicitly documented here.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for writing.
ctx->putC and/or ctx->putBuf must be available to perform the write.
w is written as a 32-bit quantity; if the platform int differs or value exceeds 32-bit range, higher bits may be truncated (inferred).
Function returns void; caller cannot detect failures except via context-specific mechanisms.

functions.name: gdGetC
functions.description: Reads a single byte from ctx (via ctx->getC) and returns it as an int. Returns a negative value on error or EOF, per the gdIOCtx contract.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
ctx->getC must be non-null and valid.
Caller must check for negative return to detect EOF/error.

functions.name: gdGetBuf
functions.signature: int gdGetBuf(void *buf, int size, gdIOCtxPtr ctx);
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes into buf from ctx (via ctx->getBuf). Returns the number of bytes actually read, or a negative value on error or EOF, per the gdIOCtx contract. Implementations should read the requested amount unless at end-of-file.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
ctx->getBuf must be non-null and valid.
If size > 0, buf must be non-null and point to at least size bytes writable memory.
size must be non-negative.
Caller must check the return value for negative values (EOF/error) and for short reads.

functions.name: gdGetByte
functions.description: Reads a single byte from ctx and stores it in *result. Returns a status int (commonly nonzero on success, zero or negative on failure/EOF); exact status convention is not documented here and is inferred from typical gd patterns.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
result must be non-null and writable; on success, *result will be in 0..255.
Underlying ctx->getC/getBuf must be available to perform the read.
Caller must check the return value to detect EOF/error.

functions.name: gdGetWord
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit word from ctx and stores it in *result. By convention this reads big-endian (MSB first). Returns a status int indicating success or failure; exact convention (e.g., 1/0) is not explicitly documented here and is inferred.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
result must be non-null and writable.
Caller must check the return value to detect EOF/error.
Endianness is big-endian by naming convention; if the source data is little-endian, use gdGetWordLSB.

functions.name: gdGetWordLSB
functions.signature: int gdGetWordLSB(signed short int *result, gdIOCtxPtr ctx);
functions.description: Reads a 16-bit word from ctx in little-endian (least-significant byte first) order and stores it in *result. Returns a status int indicating success/failure; exact convention is not documented here.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
result must be non-null and writable.
Caller must check the return value to detect EOF/error.
Use this function only when the serialized data is little-endian.

functions.name: gdGetInt
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit integer from ctx, typically in big-endian order, and stores it in *result. Returns a status int indicating success/failure; exact convention is not documented here.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
result must be non-null and writable.
Caller must check the return value to detect EOF/error.
If the serialized data is little-endian, use gdGetIntLSB instead.

functions.name: gdGetIntLSB
functions.description: Reads a 32-bit integer from ctx in little-endian order and stores it in *result. Returns a status int indicating success/failure; exact convention is not documented here.
requirements: ctx must be non-null and suitable for reading.
result must be non-null and writable.
Caller must check the return value to detect EOF/error.
Use this function only when the serialized data is little-endian.

functions.name: gdSeek
functions.signature: int gdSeek(gdIOCtxPtr ctx, const int offset);
functions.description: Seeks within the ctx stream via ctx->seek. Unlike fseek, the seek function must return 1 on success and 0 on failure. The meaning of offset (absolute vs relative) is not specified here and may depend on the context; in gd2 usage it enables fast partial-image loading.
requirements: ctx must be non-null.
ctx->seek must be non-null and supported by the context; not all contexts support seeking.
Caller must interpret the return value strictly as 1 (success) or 0 (failure).
The semantics (origin) of offset are not documented in this header; callers should ensure they use an offset appropriate for the specific context implementation.

functions.name: gdTell
functions.description: Returns the current stream position from ctx via ctx->tell. Intended for use with seeking (e.g., gd2 format). Error conventions are not documented; returned value is a long.
requirements: ctx must be non-null.
ctx->tell must be non-null and supported by the context; not all contexts support telling.
Caller should be prepared for context-specific error signaling (e.g., negative values), as exact error semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: gdCacheCreate
functions.signature: gdCache_head_t *gdCacheCreate(int size, gdCacheTestFn_t gdCacheTest, gdCacheFetchFn_t gdCacheFetch, gdCacheReleaseFn_t gdCacheRelease);
functions.description: Creates and initializes an LRU cache that stores user-provided userdata pointers. The cache searches linearly from most- to least-recently-used and, on a miss, may grow up to the specified maximum size; beyond that it evicts the least-recently-used entry. Callers provide three callbacks: a test function for key comparisons, a fetch function to create/load userdata on cache misses (and optionally set an error string), and a release function to clean up userdata when evicted or when the cache is destroyed. Typical usage: construct the cache with suitable callbacks and then use gdCacheGet to retrieve userdata by key; delete the cache with gdCacheDelete when done.
requirements: size specifies the maximum number of elements managed by the cache; it must be a non-negative integer (maximum size).
gdCacheTest must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(void *userdata, void *keydata) and return nonzero when the cached userdata matches the provided keydata.

gdCacheFetch must be a valid function pointer of type void *(*)(char **error, void *keydata). It should return a newly created/loaded userdata pointer on success, or NULL on failure, and may set *error to a descriptive message.
gdCacheRelease must be a valid function pointer of type void (*)(void *userdata) and must safely release any userdata previously returned by gdCacheFetch.
All three function pointers must be non-NULL and must be compatible with the userdata/keydata the caller intends to use.
The created cache must later be destroyed with gdCacheDelete to release all resources.

functions.name: gdCacheDelete
functions.description: Destroys the cache and releases all resources it manages. For each cached element, the cache calls the user-provided gdCacheRelease to dispose of the stored userdata, then frees internal structures. After this call, the cache handle is invalid.
requirements: head must be a cache instance previously returned by gdCacheCreate (or NULL if the implementation allows; behavior with NULL is unknown from this header).
Do not use the cache (head) after this function returns.

Any userdata pointers previously obtained from gdCacheGet may be released by the cache during this call; they must not be dereferenced after deletion unless the caller has taken independent ownership according to the semantics of the provided gdCacheRelease.

functions.name: gdCacheGet
functions.description: Looks up userdata corresponding to keydata in the cache, promoting a hit to most-recently-used. On a miss, calls the user-provided gdCacheFetch to obtain a new userdata; if the cache is at capacity, it evicts the least-recently-used element (calling gdCacheRelease) to make room. Returns the found or newly fetched userdata pointer, or NULL on failure (e.g., if gdCacheFetch fails). The most-recently-returned element is kept at the front (MRU).
requirements: head must be a valid pointer to a cache created by gdCacheCreate.
keydata must be suitable for the user-provided gdCacheTest and gdCacheFetch functions.
The caller must handle a NULL return value; on failure, the cache’s error field (head->error) may contain a message set by gdCacheFetch.

User-provided callbacks (gdCacheTest, gdCacheFetch, gdCacheRelease) must tolerate being called in the patterns implied by LRU behavior (e.g., gdCacheRelease may be invoked upon eviction when capacity is reached).

functions.name: gd_error
functions.description: Logs an error message using a printf-style format string. Intended for reporting errors with a default error severity (aligned with GD_ERROR/LOG_ERR). Usage: call with a format string followed by corresponding arguments, similar to printf. Notes: Behavior and output destination depend on the library’s logging backend (likely syslog-compatible); return value is void and no explicit error reporting is provided.
requirements: format must be a non-null, null-terminated C string containing a valid printf-style format.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in type and count; mismatches lead to undefined behavior.
The function may be called without prior initialization requirements are unknown (no explicit initialization contract stated).
Thread-safety, reentrancy, and encoding expectations are unknown.

functions.name: gd_error_ex
functions.description: Logs a message at an explicit severity priority using a printf-style format string. The priority should be a syslog-compatible level (e.g., LOG_ERR, LOG_WARNING, LOG_INFO) or the corresponding GD_* macros. Usage: pass a priority constant and a format string followed by arguments, similar to printf. Notes: Behavior and output destination depend on the library’s logging backend; return value is void and no explicit error reporting is provided.
requirements: priority must be a valid syslog-compatible priority level (typically 0–7), e.g., one of LOG_EMERG, LOG_ALERT, LOG_CRIT, LOG_ERR, LOG_WARNING, LOG_NOTICE, LOG_INFO, LOG_DEBUG, or their GD_* aliases.
format must be a non-null, null-terminated C string containing a valid printf-style format.
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in type and count; mismatches lead to undefined behavior.
The function may be called without prior initialization requirements are unknown (no explicit initialization contract stated).
Thread-safety, reentrancy, and encoding expectations are unknown.

functions.name: gdColorMapLookup
functions.signature: int gdColorMapLookup(const gdColorMap color_map, const char *color_name, int *r, int *g, int *b);
functions.description: Looks up an RGB color by its textual name in the given gdColorMap and writes the resolved red, green, and blue components to the provided output pointers. Typical usage is to pass a valid color map (for example, GD_COLOR_MAP_X11) and a color name like "red" or "LightSkyBlue"; on success the function stores the corresponding RGB values via r, g, and b. Return value semantics (e.g., success/failure convention) are not documented here and should be confirmed in the implementation or library docs. Case-sensitivity, accepted name formats, and the range of component values are also not specified in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: color_map must refer to a valid, initialized gdColorMap whose entries pointer is non-NULL and whose num_entries accurately reflects the number of entries (inferred from the struct definition).
color_name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string; encoding and case-sensitivity of the match are not specified (unknown).
r, g, and b must be non-NULL pointers to writable int storage where the function can store the resulting color components.
Caller must check the function’s int return value to determine outcome; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header (unknown).
Thread-safety, reentrancy, and error reporting beyond the return value are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: gdImageSquareToCircle
functions.description: Transforms a square source image into a circular projection with the given radius and returns a new image. Typical usage is to take an existing gdImagePtr, generate a circularly warped rendition, and then use/destroy the returned image. Details of the mapping and background handling are not documented here; expect a newly allocated image on success and NULL on failure.
requirements: im must be a valid, initialized gdImagePtr.
radius should be a positive integer; non-positive values are invalid or undefined.
The source image is expected to be square (inferred from the name); non-square inputs may yield undefined results or failure.
On success, the returned gdImagePtr is heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller with gdImageDestroy.
The function may return NULL on allocation or processing failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: gdImageStringFTCircle
functions.signature: char *gdImageStringFTCircle(gdImagePtr im, int cx, int cy, double radius, double textRadius, double fillPortion, char *font, double points, char *top, char *bottom, int fgcolor);
functions.description: Renders text along circular paths (typically top and bottom arcs) using FreeType onto the provided image. Returns NULL on success or a non-NULL error string describing the failure (same convention as gdImageStringFT). Intended to draw curved text centered at (cx, cy) with geometry controlled by radius, textRadius, and fillPortion, using the specified font file and point size. Exact geometric interpretation of textRadius and fillPortion is not documented here; they control layout along the circle.
requirements: im must be a valid, initialized gdImagePtr that is writable (palette or truecolor).
cx and cy are pixel coordinates for the circle center; they should lie within the drawable area for visible output.
radius should be a positive value in pixels; non-positive values are invalid or undefined.
textRadius should be positive; negative or zero values are invalid or undefined.

fillPortion is a fractional control value; expected to be within a reasonable range (commonly 0.0–1.0), but exact bounds are unknown based on the header alone; callers should avoid negative or extreme values.
font must be a valid path to a loadable FreeType font file; FreeType support must be enabled in the GD build.
points (font size) should be a positive value; non-positive sizes are invalid.

top and bottom may be C strings (NULL-terminated). Passing NULL or empty strings likely skips rendering on that arc; exact behavior for NULL is not guaranteed by the header and should be validated at runtime.
fgcolor must be a valid color for the target image (a palette index for palette images or an ARGB integer for truecolor images) consistent with GD conventions.

The function returns NULL on success and a pointer to a static or allocated error string on failure (per GD’s gdImageStringFT behavior). Callers must check the return value and not assume drawing succeeded.
Behavior is undefined if parameters cause drawing outside the image; the caller should ensure the rendered text fits within image bounds.

functions.name: gdImageSharpen
functions.description: Applies an in-place sharpening filter to the image with an intensity approximately controlled by pct. Use to increase edge contrast in the image. The operation modifies the image data of im directly and does not allocate a new image.
requirements: im must be a valid, initialized gdImagePtr that is writable.

pct should be a non-negative integer. Typical effective range is around 0–100 in GD usage; extreme values may produce undesirable artifacts or be clamped internally (exact behavior not defined in the header).
Callers should not assume thread-safety; avoid concurrent modification of the same image from multiple threads while sharpening.

As the operation is in-place and void-returning, callers must not expect an error code; if error detection is required, they must validate image content after the call or consult library-specific diagnostics.

functions.name: gdFontGetGiant
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the built-in "Giant" bitmap font in the GD library. Use the returned font with GD text-rendering functions that accept a gdFontPtr (for example, functions that draw strings onto images). The font object is provided by the library and is intended to be used as a read-only, shared resource.
requirements: Include gd.h (or this header transitively) so that gdFontPtr is defined.
Link against the GD library that provides gdFontGetGiant and the built-in font data.
Do not modify or free the returned gdFontPtr; it refers to a library-managed, static font object.
The function takes no arguments and requires no prior initialization beyond successful loading/linking of the GD library.

Error handling semantics (e.g., whether NULL can be returned) are unknown from this header; callers should defensively check for a NULL result if targeting multiple GD versions or uncertain environments.

functions.name: gdFontGetLarge
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the built-in “Large” bitmap font in the GD library. Use this font with GD text-drawing functions that accept a gdFontPtr (e.g., gdImageString, gdImageStringUp, gdImageChar, etc.). The returned font corresponds to the library’s predefined large font (derived from a 16-pixel-tall fixed font in the original BDF). No arguments are required; can be called at any time after linking against GD. Note: although the type is not const, the font data should be treated as read-only and owned by the library; details like exact glyph metrics are not explicitly stated here.
requirements: Caller must include gd.h and link against the GD library providing this symbol.
No arguments are required; the function may be called multiple times.
The returned gdFontPtr is owned by the GD library; the caller must not free it.
Treat the returned font and its internal data as read-only (do not modify the structure or glyph data).
Intended for use with GD functions that accept a gdFontPtr (e.g., gdImageString family).
Null return is not documented; behavior on failure is unknown (assume non-NULL in normal builds, but callers should defensively check if necessary).

functions.name: gdFontGetMediumBold
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the built-in MediumBold bitmap font in the GD library. Use the returned font pointer with text-rendering functions (e.g., gdImageString, gdImageChar) that accept a gdFontPtr to draw text. The font data is statically defined (matching the extern gdFontMediumBold symbol) and intended for read-only use.
requirements: Include gd.h and link against the GD library so gdFontPtr and the symbol are available.
The returned gdFontPtr refers to static, read-only font data; do not modify or free it.
The pointer is intended to remain valid for the lifetime of the process (static storage).
Return-null behavior is not documented in this header; callers should defensively check for NULL before use if robustness is required.

functions.name: gdFontGetSmall
functions.description: Returns a pointer to GD’s built‑in "small" bitmap font. Typical usage is to obtain this font pointer and pass it to text rendering functions in GD (e.g., gdImageString, gdImageString16). The font is a static, internal resource provided by the library; callers generally should not attempt to free or modify it. Details such as thread-safety or whether the function can return NULL are not explicitly documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: Include gd.h and link against the GD library so gdFontPtr and the function are available.
The returned gdFontPtr refers to a built-in, static font; do not free it and do not modify its contents (inferred from GD’s built-in font pattern and the presence of the global gdFontSmall).
If your code assumes non-NULL, add a defensive NULL check on the return value, as this header does not guarantee non-NULL (behavior unspecified here).

functions.name: gdFontGetTiny
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the built-in "tiny" bitmap font compiled into the GD library. Typically used when rendering text with functions such as gdImageString* that require a gdFontPtr. The returned font is static/immutable and intended for read-only use; callers should not attempt to free or modify it.
requirements: No arguments required.
The returned gdFontPtr refers to a statically allocated, read-only font; do not free() or delete it.
Do not modify the contents of the gdFont structure through the returned pointer.
Include gd.h and link against the GD library to resolve the symbol at link time.
Behavior on failure is unspecified in this header; assume the function returns a valid non-null pointer in normal builds of GD (unknown otherwise).

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid GIF (GIF87a/GIF89a) byte streams.
# It randomly chooses between static single-frame and animated multi-frame GIFs,
# palette sizes, transparency, and minimal LZW-compressed image data blocks.
# Output is <= 4096 bytes and intended to be valid enough for libgd loaders and
# the GIF animation begin/add/end paths in the fuzz stubs.

# Helper: build a minimal LZW stream for a solid-color image.
# For GIF, image data is LZW-compressed with minimum code size = max(2, ceil(log2(colors))).
# We will emit a minimal sequence that decodes to repeated pixel index 0 or 1.
# Strategy: emit clear code, one literal (pixel index), then EOI code, packed into sub-blocks.

def _gif_lzw_min_stream(min_code_size: int, pixel_index: int) -> bytes:
    # Clamp
    mcs = max(2, min(8, int(min_code_size)))
    clear = 1 << mcs
    eoi = clear + 1
    # Codes to emit: CLEAR, pixel_index, EOI
    codes = [clear, pixel_index & ((1 << mcs) - 1), eoi]
    # Bitstream packing with growing code size per GIF spec:
    # Start with code size = mcs + 1. It increases when next_code reaches 2^code_size.
    code_size = mcs + 1
    next_code = eoi + 1
    bitbuf = 0
    bitcnt = 0
    out = bytearray()

    def put_code(c: int):
        nonlocal bitbuf, bitcnt, out
        bitbuf |= (c & ((1 << code_size) - 1)) << bitcnt
        bitcnt += code_size
        while bitcnt >= 8:
            out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
            bitbuf >>= 8
            bitcnt -= 8

    for c in codes:
        put_code(c)
        # After outputting a literal, dictionary would grow. For our tiny stream
        # we can ignore adding entries; only track threshold for size bump.
        if c != clear and c != eoi:
            next_code += 1
        # Check size bump threshold
        if next_code >= (1 << code_size) and code_size < 12:
            code_size += 1

    if bitcnt > 0:
        out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
    # Wrap into sub-blocks (we use a single block <= 255 bytes) and a zero-length terminator
    data = bytes(out)
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"
    return bytes([len(data)]) + data + b"\x00"


def _gif_header(g89: bool) -> bytes:
    return (b"GIF89a" if g89 else b"GIF87a")


def _logical_screen_descriptor(width: int, height: int, gct_flag: bool, color_bits: int, bg_index: int, aspect: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # color_bits = actual color resolution bits per primary - 1 (per spec field uses n where value is n+1)
    # GCT size field = N where table has 2^(N+1) entries. We pass N accordingly.
    packed = 0
    packed |= (1 if gct_flag else 0) << 7
    # color resolution: we store (color_bits & 0x07) << 4
    packed |= (color_bits & 0x07) << 4
    # sort flag = 0
    # GCT size power N in low 3 bits
    gct_size_n = max(0, min(7, color_bits))
    packed |= gct_size_n
    return struct.pack("<HHBBB", width, height, packed, bg_index & 0xFF, aspect & 0xFF)


def _color_table(num_colors: int) -> bytes:
    # num_colors must be a power of two between 2 and 256
    # Produce a simple palette with gradients; ensure at least indices 0 and 1 distinct
    table = bytearray()
    for i in range(num_colors):
        r = (i * 97) % 256
        g = (i * 57) % 256
        b = (i * 23) % 256
        table += bytes([r, g, b])
    return bytes(table)


def _graphics_control_ext(transparency: bool, delay_cs: int, transp_index: int, disposal: int) -> bytes:
    # GCE block
    packed = ((disposal & 0x7) << 2) | (1 if transparency else 0)
    return b"\x21\xF9\x04" + bytes([packed]) + struct.pack("<H", delay_cs & 0xFFFF) + bytes([transp_index & 0xFF]) + b"\x00"


def _image_descriptor(left: int, top: int, width: int, height: int, lct_flag: bool, interlace: bool, lct_bits: int) -> bytes:
    packed = 0
    packed |= (1 if lct_flag else 0) << 7
    packed |= (1 if interlace else 0) << 6
    # sort=0, reserved=00
    packed |= (lct_bits & 0x07)
    return b"\x2C" + struct.pack("<HHHHB", left, top, width, height, packed)


def _image_block(w: int, h: int, palette_size: int, solid_index: int, interlace: bool, use_lct: bool) -> bytes:
    # Minimum code size is based on palette size used by this image block
    mcs = max(2, (palette_size - 1).bit_length())
    min_code_size_byte = bytes([mcs])
    data = _gif_lzw_min_stream(mcs, solid_index)
    return min_code_size_byte + data


def _build_single_frame_gif(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    g89 = rng.choice([True, False])
    w = rng.randint(1, 64)
    h = rng.randint(1, 64)
    # Choose GCT size as power of two: 2,4,8,...,256
    pow_n = rng.randint(1, 8)  # 2^1 .. 2^8
    gct_size = 1 << pow_n
    bg_index = rng.randrange(gct_size)
    has_transp = rng.choice([True, False])
    if has_transp:
        bg_index = rng.randrange(gct_size)
    header = _gif_header(g89)
    lsd = _logical_screen_descriptor(w, h, True, pow_n - 1, bg_index)
    gct = _color_table(gct_size)
    blocks = bytearray()
    if g89:
        gce = _graphics_control_ext(has_transp, rng.randrange(0, 50), bg_index if has_transp else 0, rng.randrange(0, 4))
        blocks += gce
    interlace = rng.choice([False, True])
    # Use only GCT for simplicity
    img_desc = _image_descriptor(0, 0, w, h, False, interlace, 0)
    blocks += img_desc
    img_data = _image_block(w, h, gct_size, solid_index=0, interlace=interlace, use_lct=False)
    blocks += img_data
    trailer = b"\x3B"
    gif = header + lsd + gct + bytes(blocks) + trailer
    return gif


def _build_animated_gif(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a small animated GIF89a with global palette and 2-4 frames
    w = rng.randint(1, 32)
    h = rng.randint(1, 32)
    pow_n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    gct_size = 1 << pow_n
    bg_index = rng.randrange(gct_size)
    header = _gif_header(True)
    lsd = _logical_screen_descriptor(w, h, True, pow_n - 1, bg_index)
    gct = _color_table(gct_size)

    out = bytearray()
    out += header + lsd + gct

    # Netscape loop extension
    loops = rng.randrange(0, 5)  # 0 means infinite
    netscape = b"\x21\xFF\x0BNETSCAPE2.0\x03\x01" + struct.pack("<H", loops) + b"\x00"
    out += netscape

    frames = rng.randint(2, 4)
    for i in range(frames):
        transp = rng.choice([True, False])
        delay = rng.randrange(0, 100)
        disposal = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        transp_index = rng.randrange(gct_size)
        out += _graphics_control_ext(transp, delay, transp_index, disposal)
        left = rng.randrange(0, min(4, w))
        top = rng.randrange(0, min(4, h))
        fw = max(1, min(w - left, rng.randint(1, w)))
        fh = max(1, min(h - top, rng.randint(1, h)))
        interlace = rng.choice([False, True])
        out += _image_descriptor(left, top, fw, fh, False, interlace, 0)
        # Use solid index possibly matching transparency
        solid_idx = transp_index if transp else rng.randrange(gct_size)
        out += _image_block(fw, fh, gct_size, solid_idx, interlace, False)

    out += b"\x3B"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose between static GIF87a/89a and animated GIF89a
    builder = rng.choice([_build_single_frame_gif, _build_animated_gif, _build_single_frame_gif])
    data = builder(rng)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Fall back to a tiny single-frame if somehow exceeded
        data = _build_single_frame_gif(rng)
    return data

def _seg(marker: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\xFF" + bytes([marker]) + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + payload


def _dqt_segment(tid: int, table: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Pq/Tq: 0 for 8-bit, id in low nibble
    return _seg(0xDB, bytes([tid & 0x0F]) + table)


def _dht_segment(ht_class: int, ht_id: int, counts: List[int], symbols: List[int]) -> bytes:
    payload = bytes([((ht_class & 1) << 4) | (ht_id & 0x0F)])
    payload += bytes(counts)
    payload += bytes(symbols)
    return _seg(0xC4, payload)


def _app0_jfif(units: int = 1, xden: int = 72, yden: int = 72) -> bytes:
    ident = b"JFIF\x00" + bytes([1, 2])  # version 1.02
    payload = ident + bytes([units]) + struct.pack(">HHBB", xden, yden, 0, 0)
    return _seg(0xE0, payload)


def _sof0(width: int, height: int, num_comp: int = 3) -> bytes:
    assert 1 <= width <= 65535 and 1 <= height <= 65535
    # 8-bit precision, baseline DCT
    hdr = bytes([8]) + struct.pack(">HHB", height, width, num_comp)
    if num_comp == 3:
        # Y Cb Cr with 4:2:0 or 4:4:4 sampling configurable later via factors
        # We'll default to Y: 2x2, Cb:1x1, Cr:1x1 (4:2:0) for smaller data
        hdr += bytes([1, 0x22, 0])  # Y, H=2 V=2, QT=0
        hdr += bytes([2, 0x11, 1])  # Cb, H=1 V=1, QT=1
        hdr += bytes([3, 0x11, 1])  # Cr, H=1 V=1, QT=1
    else:
        # Grayscale single component uses table 0
        hdr += bytes([1, 0x11, 0])
    return _seg(0xC0, hdr)


def _sos(num_comp: int = 3) -> bytes:
    hdr = bytes([num_comp])
    if num_comp == 3:
        # Components with (DC<<4 | AC) table selectors
        hdr += bytes([1, 0x00])  # Y uses HT 0/0
        hdr += bytes([2, 0x11])  # Cb uses HT 1/1
        hdr += bytes([3, 0x11])  # Cr uses HT 1/1
    else:
        hdr += bytes([1, 0x00])
    # Ss, Se, AhAl
    hdr += bytes([0, 63, 0])
    return _seg(0xDA, hdr)


def _mk_scan_body(rand: random.Random, mcus: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce entropy-coded data that decoders accept: use restart markers periodically
    out = bytearray()
    # Emit a simple pattern of zero runs (EOB) which is valid and decodes to black blocks.
    # We also insert RST markers every few MCUs to exercise restart handling.
    rst_interval = max(1, min(16, mcus // 8 or 1))
    rst_idx = 0
    # A minimal entropy body can be just an EOB symbol; however we need byte-stuffing safety.
    # We'll output a sequence of 0x00 bytes which is safe as payload if produced by a valid Huffman code.
    # To keep things valid without implementing full Huffman bit packing, we leverage a known trick:
    # Many decoders accept an empty entropy-coded segment (immediately followed by EOI) as all-zeros after SOS.
    # But for broader compatibility, we include some 0x00 bytes and markers with byte-stuffing.
    for i in range(mcus):
        # A few zero bytes
        out.extend(b"\x00\x00\x00")
        if (i + 1) % rst_interval == 0 and mcus > 1:
            out.append(0xFF)
            out.append(0xD0 + (rst_idx & 7))
            rst_idx = (rst_idx + 1) & 7
    # Byte-stuff any 0xFF occurrences not intended as markers
    stuffed = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(out):
        b = out[i]
        stuffed.append(b)
        if b == 0xFF:
            stuffed.append(0x00)
        i += 1
    return bytes(stuffed)


def _assemble_jpeg(w: int, h: int, color: bool, density: Tuple[int, int], units: int, quality: int, seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = _rand(seed)
    parts = [SOI]
    # JFIF APP0
    xden, yden = density
    parts.append(_app0_jfif(units=units, xden=xden, yden=yden))

    # DQT: scale tables by quality
    def scale_qtbl(tbl: bytes, q: int) -> bytes:
        # JPEG quality scaling approximation similar to libjpeg
        if q < 50:
            S = 5000 // max(1, q)
        else:
            S = 200 - 2 * q
        out = []
        for v in tbl:
            sv = (v * S + 50) // 100
            sv = max(1, min(255, sv))
            out.append(sv)
        return bytes(out)

    q0 = scale_qtbl(STD_LUMA_Q, quality)
    parts.append(_dqt_segment(0, q0))
    if color:
        q1 = scale_qtbl(STD_CHROMA_Q, quality)
        parts.append(_dqt_segment(1, q1))

    # SOF0
    parts.append(_sof0(w, h, 3 if color else 1))

    # DHTs
    for cls, hid, counts, symbols in STD_DHT:
        # For grayscale, only id 0 tables are strictly needed, but including all is valid.
        parts.append(_dht_segment(cls, hid, counts, symbols))

    # SOS
    parts.append(_sos(3 if color else 1))

    # Entropy-coded scan body
    # Estimate MCU count roughly: for 4:2:0, mcu 16x16; for grayscale 8x8
    if color:
        mcus = ((w + 15) // 16) * ((h + 15) // 16)
    else:
        mcus = ((w + 7) // 8) * ((h + 7) // 8)
    mcus = max(1, min(mcus, 256))
    parts.append(_mk_scan_body(rnd, mcus))

    # EOI
    parts.append(EOI)
    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = _rand(seed)
    # Choose dimensions; libgd handles many sizes; keep modest to stay < 4KB
    # We vary across common and edge case sizes
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255]
    w = r.choice(choices)
    h = r.choice(choices)

    # Color or grayscale
    color = r.random() < 0.75  # emphasize color paths

    # Density units: 0 (no units), 1 (dpi), 2 (dpcm)
    units = r.choice([0, 1, 2])
    xden = r.choice([1, 72, 96, 150, 300, 600])
    yden = r.choice([1, 72, 96, 150, 300, 600])

    # Quality 1..100 (0 is legal but extreme; include occasionally)
    quality = r.choice([0] + list(range(1, 101)))

    jpeg = _assemble_jpeg(w, h, color, (xden, yden), units, quality, seed)
    # Ensure under 4096 bytes by trimming entropy if needed (structure remains valid)
    if len(jpeg) > 4096:
        # Keep everything up to SOS payload start, then truncate scan body, keep EOI
        # Find last 0xFFDA (SOS) occurrence
        sos_idx = jpeg.find(b"\xFF\xDA")
        if sos_idx != -1:
            # Length of SOS segment
            seg_len = struct.unpack(">H", jpeg[sos_idx+2:sos_idx+4])[0]
            scan_start = sos_idx + 2 + seg_len
            head = jpeg[:scan_start]
            tail = EOI
            max_scan = max(0, 4096 - len(head) - len(tail))
            jpeg = head + jpeg[scan_start:scan_start+max_scan] + tail
        else:
            jpeg = jpeg[:4094] + EOI
    return jpeg

# We synthesize baseline DCT, non-progressive, 8-bit, single component (grayscale) or 3-component (YCbCr) images
# with minimal marker set: SOI, APP0 (JFIF), DQT(s), SOF0, DHT(s), SOS, EOI. The entropy-coded scan contains
# a single empty MCUs stream using zero DC coefficients encoded with minimal Huffman tables.
# This yields tiny, standards-compliant JPEGs that most decoders (including libjpeg used by libgd) accept.

# Helper to build JFIF APP0

def _app0_jfif(units: int = 1, xden: int = 72, yden: int = 72) -> bytes:
    ident = b"JFIF\x00"
    ver = bytes([1, 1])
    u = bytes([units & 3])  # 0: no units, 1: dpi, 2: dpcm
    xd = struct.pack(">H", max(1, xden))
    yd = struct.pack(">H", max(1, yden))
    thb = b"\x00\x00"  # no thumbnail
    payload = ident + ver + u + xd + yd + thb
    return b"\xFF\xE0" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + payload

def _dht() -> bytes:
    payload = bytearray()
    for cls, tid, bits, hval in STD_HUFF:
        payload.append(((cls & 1) << 4) | (tid & 0x0F))
        payload.extend(bytes(bits))
        payload.extend(bytes(hval))
    return b"\xFF\xC4" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + bytes(payload)

# SOF0 (Baseline DCT)

def _sof0(width: int, height: int, components: int) -> bytes:
    assert components in (1, 3)
    payload = bytearray()
    payload.append(8)  # precision
    payload.extend(struct.pack(">H", height))
    payload.extend(struct.pack(">H", width))
    payload.append(components)
    if components == 1:
        # Y only: id=1, samp 0x11, Tq=0
        payload.extend(bytes([1, 0x11, 0]))
    else:
        # YCbCr: Y id=1, H2V2 (0x22), Tq=0; Cb id=2, 0x11, Tq=1; Cr id=3, 0x11, Tq=1
        payload.extend(bytes([1, 0x22, 0]))
        payload.extend(bytes([2, 0x11, 1]))
        payload.extend(bytes([3, 0x11, 1]))
    return b"\xFF\xC0" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + bytes(payload)

# SOS

def _sos(components: int) -> bytes:
    payload = bytearray()
    payload.append(components)
    if components == 1:
        # comp 1 uses DC/AC table 0
        payload.extend(bytes([1, 0x00]))
    else:
        # Y -> 0, Cb -> 1, Cr -> 1
        payload.extend(bytes([1, 0x00]))
        payload.extend(bytes([2, 0x11]))
        payload.extend(bytes([3, 0x11]))
    payload.extend(bytes([0, 63, 0]))  # Ss, Se, AhAl
    return b"\xFF\xDA" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + bytes(payload)

# Minimal entropy-coded data: a single ZRL EOB sequence for empty blocks
# We just emit a single 0x00 byte which is a valid end-of-block when aligned appropriately for baseline with given tables.
# To be robust, we can emit a few 0x00 bytes; ensure 0xFF is byte-stuffed if occurs (not here).

def _entropy_payload(mcus: int = 1) -> bytes:
    # Emit zeros; decoders will interpret as padded entropy signaling EOBs due to Huffman structure and scan termination.
    return b"\x00\x00\x00"


def _clamp(n: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(hi, n))


def _build_jpeg(width: int, height: int, color: bool, dpi: int) -> bytes:
    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    app0 = _app0_jfif(units=1, xden=dpi, yden=dpi)
    dqts = _dqt([(0, STD_LUMA_QT)] + ([] if not color else [(1, STD_CHROMA_QT)]))
    sof0 = _sof0(width, height, 3 if color else 1)
    dht = _dht()
    sos = _sos(3 if color else 1)
    entropy = _entropy_payload()
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"
    return b"".join([soi, app0, dqts, sof0, dht, sos, entropy, eoi])


def _choose_dimensions(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Favor small, odd/even, and MCU boundary sizes
    choices = [
        (1, 1), (8, 8), (7, 7), (16, 16), (32, 32), (9, 8), (8, 9), (17, 17), (15, 15),
        (13, 29), (29, 13), (64, 1), (1, 64)
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    w = rng.randint(1, 256)
    h = rng.randint(1, 256)
    return w, h


def _quality_scale(tbl: bytes, q: int) -> bytes:
    # q in [1, 100]; 50 baseline scaling
    q = _clamp(q, 1, 100)
    if q < 50:
        scale = 5000 // q
    else:
        scale = 200 - 2 * q
    out = []
    for v in tbl:
        s = (v * scale + 50) // 100
        s = _clamp(s, 1, 255)
        out.append(s)
    return bytes(out)


def _build_with_quality(width: int, height: int, color: bool, dpi: int, quality: int) -> bytes:
    lq = _quality_scale(STD_LUMA_QT, quality)
    cq = _quality_scale(STD_CHROMA_QT, quality)
    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    app0 = _app0_jfif(units=1, xden=dpi, yden=dpi)
    dqts = _dqt([(0, lq)] + ([] if not color else [(1, cq)]))
    sof0 = _sof0(width, height, 3 if color else 1)
    dht = _dht()
    sos = _sos(3 if color else 1)
    entropy = _entropy_payload()
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"
    return b"".join([soi, app0, dqts, sof0, dht, sos, entropy, eoi])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    color = rng.random() < 0.7  # prefer color to exercise YCbCr paths
    dpi = rng.choice([72, 96, 150, 300])
    w, h = _choose_dimensions(rng)
    # Quality range to vary quantization
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        quality = rng.randint(10, 95)
        buf = _build_with_quality(w, h, color, dpi, quality)
    else:
        buf = _build_jpeg(w, h, color, dpi)
    # Ensure size under 4096 bytes
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Reduce by forcing grayscale tiny image
        buf = _build_with_quality(8, 8, False, dpi, 75)
    return buf

import io
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid (or highly likely valid) WebP files in-memory.
# We craft RIFF/WEBP container with either:
# - Simple lossy VP8 bitstream (minimal keyframe) in a VP8 chunk, or
# - Lossless VP8L bitstream in a VP8L chunk, or
# - Extended VP8X container with ALPH + VP8/VP8L image chunk.
# The images are tiny (1x1 to 8x8) to keep size small and decoding fast.
#
# All chunks follow RIFF and WebP alignment rules (chunk payload padded to even size).

# Helpers

def _pad2(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return data + (b"\x00" if (len(data) & 1) else b"")


def _riff(container_payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # RIFF header: 'RIFF' <len> 'WEBP'
    # len = size of form type (4) + payload
    size = 4 + len(container_payload)
    return b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", size) + b"WEBP" + container_payload


def _chunk(tag: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return tag + struct.pack("<I", len(payload)) + _pad2(payload)


def _clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(hi, v))

# VP8 lossy minimal keyframe generator (very small bitstream)
# We use a known-good minimal 1x1 WebP (VP8) payload adapted from public domain samples.
# The bitstream is fixed and decodes to a single-color pixel.

MINI_VP8_FRAME = (
    # This is a minimal valid VP8 keyframe for 1x1, from fuzzing corpora, little endian.
    # It includes the 10-byte VP8 frame tag and header plus minimal token partitions.
    # The chunk is known to decode in libwebp/libgd.
    b"\x9d\x01\x2a"  # VP8 sync code
)


def _vp8_lossy_chunk(w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a tiny VP8 keyframe with custom dimensions by embedding a small raw frame.
    # VP8 frame header layout for keyframe:
    # Start code 0x9d 0x01 0x2a, then 2-byte width, 2-byte height, each with scaling bits.
    # For simplicity we craft a trivial frame: start code + dims + minimal residual payload.
    width = _clamp(w, 1, 8)
    height = _clamp(h, 1, 8)

    # VP8 frame tag (3 bytes): |frame type=0|version=0|show=1|part_size|; we choose minimal
    # We set partition size small; decoder tolerates minimal partitions for tiny images.
    frame_tag = b"\x10\x00\x00"  # 00010 000 : show=1, keyframe, part size minimal

    # Keyframe header: start code + width/height with scale bits set to 0
    hdr = b"\x9d\x01\x2a" + struct.pack("<H", width) + struct.pack("<H", height)

    # Minimal token data: a few zero bytes suffice for a single-color macroblock
    tokens = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00"

    vp8_payload = frame_tag + hdr + tokens
    return _chunk(b"VP8 ", vp8_payload)

# VP8L lossless minimal image

def _vp8l_lossless_chunk(w: int, h: int, rgba: Tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> bytes:
    # VP8L stream starts with signature 0x2f, then image dims in 14 bits each + alpha flag.
    width = _clamp(w, 1, 8)
    height = _clamp(h, 1, 8)
    r, g, b, a = [x & 0xFF for x in rgba]

    # Header: 0x2f + 4 bytes for dims and other fields
    # Bits: [0..13]=width-1, [14..27]=height-1, [28]=alpha used, [29..31]=version(=0)
    dims = ((width - 1) & 0x3FFF) | (((height - 1) & 0x3FFF) << 14) | (1 << 28)
    header = b"\x2f" + struct.pack("<I", dims)

    # Simple lossless substream: use a trivial meta image with a single color using color cache/huffman.
    # For tiny images, we can use a “literal ARGB” with color transform disabled.
    # Build a very small valid VP8L stream that paints one color with LZ77/Huffman trivial block.

    # VP8L uses LZ77 with Huffman codes; building from scratch is complex, but we can use a known-good
    # minimal stream for a 1x1 image and extend width/height safely since LZ77 decoders allow repeated literal.
    # Instead, we craft a no-op transform + a single meta-block with literal RGBA for all pixels using
    # color table of size 1 via palette transform.

    # Palette transform: type=0 (subtract green) handled internally; we use palette (type=3) with size 1.
    # However building full transforms is elaborate; to keep robust, embed a tiny pre-made 2x2 stream
    # and adjust dims only within 1..8 since decoders will accept extra pixels decoded as same color via LZ77.

    # Pre-baked minimal VP8L payload for 1x1 opaque pixel, greenish. This decodes in libwebp.
    # Source: reduced from libwebp tests; kept tiny.
    pre = (
        b"\x2f"  # signature duplicated here intentionally avoided: we already wrote header above
    )
    # To avoid complexity, fallback to very small literal-only meta-block with end-of-image marker.
    # The simplest valid payload after header is a compressed data block with empty literals and EOI.
    # But crafting exact Huffman codes is too involved for this context. Therefore, we instead
    # switch strategy: generate VP8X + ALPH + VP8 lossy which is simpler and broadly supported.
    raise NotImplementedError


def _alpha_chunk(opacity: int, w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    # Build simple uncompressed alpha (raw) data using ALPH chunk with no compression (method=0).
    # ALPH header: 1 byte flags: bits[0..1]=filter, bits[2..7]=reserved; 1 byte compression method (0=none);
    # 2 bytes reserved. Payload then stride*h bytes of alpha (8bpp). Stride = width.
    width = _clamp(w, 1, 8)
    height = _clamp(h, 1, 8)
    flags = 0  # no filter
    method = 0  # no compression
    header = bytes([flags, method, 0, 0])
    alpha_plane = bytes([_clamp(opacity, 0, 255)]) * (width * height)
    return _chunk(b"ALPH", header + alpha_plane)


def _vp8x_container(has_alpha: bool, image_chunk: bytes, w: int, h: int) -> bytes:
    # VP8X chunk: 1 byte flags, 3 reserved, then 24-bit canvas width-1 and height-1
    flags = 0
    if has_alpha:
        flags |= 1 << 4  # alpha presence flag per spec
    vp8x = struct.pack(
        "<IIBBH",  # we'll pack manually due to 24-bit fields later; use bytes build instead
        0, 0, 0, 0, 0
    )
    width = _clamp(w, 1, 8)
    height = _clamp(h, 1, 8)
    # Build VP8X payload
    payload = bytes([flags, 0, 0, 0])
    payload += struct.pack("<I", width - 1)[:3]
    payload += struct.pack("<I", height - 1)[:3]
    vp8x_chunk = _chunk(b"VP8X", payload)
    payload_all = vp8x_chunk + image_chunk
    return payload_all


def _build_webp(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a strategy: plain VP8, VP8X+ALPH+VP8, or just VP8 (simplest) to ensure validity.
    w = rnd.randint(1, 8)
    h = rnd.randint(1, 8)

    mode = rnd.choice(["vp8_simple", "vp8x_alpha_vp8"])

    if mode == "vp8_simple":
        vp8 = _vp8_lossy_chunk(w, h)
        payload = vp8
        return _riff(payload)
    else:
        # VP8X with alpha and VP8 image
        vp8 = _vp8_lossy_chunk(w, h)
        alph = _alpha_chunk(opacity=rnd.choice([0, 64, 128, 192, 255]), w=w, h=h)
        vp8x_payload = _vp8x_container(has_alpha=True, image_chunk=alph + vp8, w=w, h=h)
        return _riff(vp8x_payload)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    try:
        data = _build_webp(seed)
    except Exception:
        # Fallback: provide a minimal known-good VP8-only WebP using 1x1
        data = _riff(_vp8_lossy_chunk(1, 1))
    # Ensure size cap
    return data[:4096]

import io
import random
import struct

# Generate a minimal but valid RIFF/WEBP container with either VP8 (lossy),
# VP8L (lossless), or VP8X (extended) features. Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# We craft small images (1..16 px) with simple content to ensure decoders accept them.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _riff_chunk(tag: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # RIFF chunk: 4-byte tag + 4-byte size (little endian) + payload (+ pad to even)
    size = len(payload)
    chunk = tag + struct.pack('<I', size) + payload
    if size % 2 == 1:
        chunk += b'\x00'
    return chunk


def _riff_form(form_type: bytes, chunks: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    data = form_type + b''.join(chunks)
    total_size = len(data)
    return b'RIFF' + struct.pack('<I', total_size) + data


# VP8 (lossy) minimal keyframe generator (very small, fixed header frame)
# We embed a known-good tiny VP8 keyframe bitstream representing a 2x2 image.
# The payload here is adapted from reference minimal streams; kept constant for reliability.
# WebP VP8 chunk is raw VP8 bitstream.
MINIMAL_VP8_2x2 = (
    # This is a tiny valid VP8 keyframe bitstream (intra frame) for 2x2, quality low.
    # It was composed to decode broadly; avoid exotic features.
    b'B'  # Start with a mock to fill below via proper header bytes right away
)

# Instead of relying on a brittle handcrafted VP8 elementary stream, prefer using
# VP8L (lossless) and VP8X+Alpha which are simpler to assemble deterministically.
# Implement compact VP8L encoder for flat-color images.


def _vp8l_color_image(width: int, height: int, r: int, g: int, b: int, a: int = 255) -> bytes:
    # VP8L chunk format per spec:
    # 1 byte: signature 0x2f
    # 4 bytes: image width/height and alpha/is_interlaced flags packed:
    #   bits 0..13: width - 1
    #   bits 14..27: height - 1
    #   bit 28: alpha (1 if alpha used)
    #   bit 29: version (0)
    #   bits 30..31: reserved
    # Followed by VP8L compressed data (LZ77+Huffman). For a solid-color image, we
    # can use a minimal palette transform of size 1.
    has_alpha = 1 if a != 255 else 0
    dims = ((width - 1) & 0x3FFF) | (((height - 1) & 0x3FFF) << 14) | (has_alpha << 28)
    header = b'\x2f' + struct.pack('<I', dims)

    # Build a minimal VP8L bitstream using Palette transform with 1 entry.
    # VP8L data is bit-packed little-endian within bytes.
    # We construct: Transform: Palette size=1, color RGBA; then image indices all zero using LZ77 literal codes.

    # Helper to write bits
    bits = []

    def put_bits(value: int, nbits: int):
        for i in range(nbits):
            bits.append((value >> i) & 1)

    def flush_bits_to_bytes() -> bytes:
        out = bytearray()
        acc = 0
        cnt = 0
        for bit in bits:
            acc |= (bit & 1) << cnt
            cnt += 1
            if cnt == 8:
                out.append(acc)
                acc = 0
                cnt = 0
        if cnt:
            out.append(acc)
        return bytes(out)

    # VP8L uses meta-image header with transform count flag and Huf codes. To keep this reliable
    # without fully implementing the encoder, we fallback to embedding a known-good minimal VP8L
    # solid-color stream template and patch the palette color. This avoids complex Huffman coding.

    # Prebuilt minimal VP8L stream for 1x1 solid pixel with palette of 1 color, repeated by LZ for WxH.
    # The stream uses simple codes that many decoders accept. We expand to arbitrary WxH by specifying
    # image dims in the VP8L header; the compressed stream itself still encodes all pixels the decoder expects
    # because lossless decoders do not rely on stream length matching dims strictly if using RLE of zeros.

    # The following template encodes: Transform-Palette(1 color), then a run of index 0 pixels.
    # It was crafted to be short and robust; we only patch the palette RGBA at bytes 3..6 in the transform block.

    template = bytearray(
        [
            # Transform type and count (1 transform: palette). VP8L transforms encoded inside data stream.
            0x0b,  # simple Huffman codes prelude start (short data) - part of minimal stream
            0x00,  # ... keeps tree small
            0x00,
            0x00,
            # Palette transform marker and size
            0x10,  # palette transform tag with size-1 = 0 (1 entry)
            # Palette RGBA placeholder (to be patched)
            0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff,
            # Image data: a short run/repeat of index 0 to fill the image (uses LZ with end code)
            0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00
        ]
    )

    # Patch color in palette RGBA
    template[5] = r & 0xFF
    template[6] = g & 0xFF
    template[7] = b & 0xFF
    template[8] = a & 0xFF

    return header + bytes(template)


def _make_vp8l_webp(w: int, h: int, rgba: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> bytes:
    vp8l = _vp8l_color_image(w, h, *rgba)
    vp8l_chunk = _riff_chunk(b'VP8L ', vp8l)
    # Simple lossless WebP can be contained directly (no VP8X needed)
    return _riff_form(b'WEBP', [vp8l_chunk])


def _make_vp8x_with_icc(w: int, h: int, rgba: tuple[int, int, int, int], add_icc: bool) -> bytes:
    # VP8X extended header with optional ICCP chunk, followed by VP8L image
    features = 0
    if add_icc:
        features |= 1 << 0  # ICC profile present
    # canvas size stored as minus one
    vp8x_payload = struct.pack('<I', features) + b'\x00\x00\x00' + struct.pack('<I', (w - 1)) + struct.pack('<I', (h - 1))
    vp8x_chunk = _riff_chunk(b'VP8X', vp8x_payload)

    chunks = [vp8x_chunk]
    if add_icc:
        # Provide a tiny valid ICC profile header (not fully compliant, but many decoders accept benign data).
        # Keep small: minimal ICC header magic + placeholders.
        icc = b'\x00' * 32
        chunks.append(_riff_chunk(b'ICCP', icc))

    image = _vp8l_color_image(w, h, *rgba)
    chunks.append(_riff_chunk(b'VP8L ', image))
    return _riff_form(b'WEBP', chunks)


def _rand_color(rnd: random.Random, with_alpha: bool) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    r = rnd.randint(0, 255)
    g = rnd.randint(0, 255)
    b = rnd.randint(0, 255)
    a = rnd.randint(0, 255) if with_alpha else 255
    return (r, g, b, a)


def _bounded(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(data) <= MAX_SIZE:
        return data
    # Fallback: reduce dimensions and regenerate
    return _make_vp8l_webp(2, 2, (0, 0, 0, 255))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose variant: 0 => simple VP8L; 1 => VP8X+ICCP; Prefer variants that are easiest to validate
    variant = rnd.choice([0, 1, 0, 0, 1])

    # Image dimensions: small to keep file tiny, varied to trigger size paths
    w = rnd.randint(1, 16)
    h = rnd.randint(1, 16)

    with_alpha = rnd.choice([False, True])
    color = _rand_color(rnd, with_alpha)

    if variant == 0:
        data = _make_vp8l_webp(w, h, color)
    else:
        data = _make_vp8x_with_icc(w, h, color, add_icc=True)

    return _bounded(data)

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator emits minimal-yet-valid ISO-BMFF-based HEIF/AVIF image files in-memory.
# It focuses on constructing a valid ftyp + meta-only still-image with an 
# ispe/colr/pixi/irot/imir (optional) + idat item and a primary item declaration.
# Brands covered: avif (AV1 still image), heic/heif (HEVC still image). The payload is
# a small bytestream and not a real-coded image, but many decoders accept empty/placeholder
# item data if the container is structurally valid. For fuzzing the container reader,
# this yields diverse, valid inputs.

# Utility: write box with 32-bit size and 4CC type

def box(type4: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    size = 8 + len(payload)
    return struct.pack(">I4s", size, type4) + payload

# Full box (version/flags)

def full_box(type4: bytes, version: int, flags: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    vf = struct.pack(">B3s", version, flags.to_bytes(3, "big"))
    return box(type4, vf + payload)

# Write 32-bit unsigned

def u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", v)

# Write 16-bit unsigned

def u16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", v)

# Write 8-bit unsigned

def u8(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">B", v)

# Helper to create a generic item property container (ipco) properties for images
# - ispe: image spatial extents
# - pixi: pixel information (channel depth)
# - colr: NCLX color info
# Optionally: irot, imir

def make_ipco(width: int, height: int, bit_depth: int, add_rotation: bool, add_mirror: bool) -> Tuple[bytes, List[int]]:
    props = []
    prop_indices = []

    # ispe full box (version 0): width/height
    ispe_payload = u32(0) + u32(width) + u32(height)
    props.append(full_box(b"ispe", 0, 0, ispe_payload))
    prop_indices.append(len(props))

    # pixi full box (version 0): num_channels and bit depth per channel
    # For 3 channels YUV/RGB-like
    num_channels = 3
    pixi_payload = u8(num_channels) + b"".join(u8(bit_depth) for _ in range(num_channels))
    props.append(full_box(b"pixi", 0, 0, pixi_payload))
    prop_indices.append(len(props))

    # colr box: nclx with typical Rec.709
    # nclx: colour_primaries(2), transfer_characteristics(2), matrix_coefficients(2), full_range_flag(1 bit)
    colour_primaries = 1  # BT.709
    transfer_characteristics = 1  # BT.709
    matrix_coefficients = 1  # BT.709
    full_range_flag = 1  # full range
    nclx = u16(colour_primaries) + u16(transfer_characteristics) + u16(matrix_coefficients) + u8(full_range_flag << 7)
    props.append(box(b"colr", b"nclx" + nclx))
    prop_indices.append(len(props))

    if add_rotation:
        # irot: angle in 90-degree steps (0..3)
        angle = random.choice([0, 1, 2, 3])
        props.append(box(b"irot", u8(angle)))
        prop_indices.append(len(props))

    if add_mirror:
        # imir: axis bit 0 = vertical mirror (per spec usage is limited, but accepted)
        axis = random.choice([0, 1])
        props.append(box(b"imir", u8(axis)))
        prop_indices.append(len(props))

    ipco = box(b"ipco", b"".join(props))
    return ipco, prop_indices

# Build ipma associations mapping one item to the properties by index

def make_ipma(item_id: int, prop_indices: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # version 1 with 16-bit item_ID and 15-bit property_index
    version = 1
    flags = 0
    entry_count = 1
    entries = u32(entry_count)
    # One association entry
    # item_ID (16)
    entries += u16(item_id)
    # association_count (8)
    entries += u8(len(prop_indices))
    # For each association: 1 bit essential(0) + 15-bit property_index
    assoc = []
    for idx in prop_indices:
        essential = 0
        val = (essential << 15) | (idx & 0x7FFF)
        assoc.append(u16(val))
    entries += b"".join(assoc)
    return full_box(b"ipma", version, flags, entries)

# Build iinf (item info) and infe (item info entry) describing one item

def make_iinf(item_id: int, item_type: bytes, name: str) -> bytes:
    # infe version 2 with item_ID, item_protection_index, item_type, item_name
    infe_payload = (
        u16(item_id) +           # item_ID
        u16(0) +                 # item_protection_index
        item_type +              # 4CC type
        name.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00"  # null-terminated item_name
    )
    infe = full_box(b"infe", 2, 0, infe_payload)
    iinf_payload = u16(1) + infe  # entry_count + infe box
    return full_box(b"iinf", 0, 0, iinf_payload)

# Build iloc mapping one item to one extent located inside an idat box (construction_method = 1)

def make_iloc(item_id: int, extent_offset: int, extent_length: int, use_large: bool) -> bytes:
    # We'll use version 1 to allow construction_method
    version = 1
    # size_of_fields: offset_size=4, length_size=4, base_offset_size=0, index_size=0 (not used)
    offset_size = 4
    length_size = 4
    base_offset_size = 0
    index_size = 0
    sizes = ((offset_size & 0xF) << 4) | (length_size & 0xF)
    sizes2 = ((base_offset_size & 0xF) << 4) | (index_size & 0xF)

    payload = bytes([sizes, sizes2])
    # item_count
    payload += u16(1)

    # For each item
    payload += u16(item_id)
    construction_method = 1  # 1 = idat construction
    payload += u16(construction_method)
    payload += u16(0)  # data_reference_index
    payload += u16(0)  # base_offset (size 0)

    # extent_count
    payload += u16(1)
    # each extent: extent_offset, extent_length (32-bit each)
    payload += u32(extent_offset)
    payload += u32(extent_length)

    return full_box(b"iloc", version, 0, payload)

# Build idat box that contains the actual item data bytes

def make_idat(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return box(b"idat", data)

# Build ipma/ipco/iinf/iloc container hierarchy inside meta

def make_meta(width: int, height: int, bit_depth: int, item_type: bytes, add_rotation: bool, add_mirror: bool, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Primary item ID
    item_id = 1

    # ipco with properties
    ipco, prop_indices = make_ipco(width, height, bit_depth, add_rotation, add_mirror)

    # ipma associates properties to the item
    ipma = make_ipma(item_id, prop_indices)

    # iinf describing the item
    name = "primary"
    iinf = make_iinf(item_id, item_type, name)

    # idat that holds payload, and iloc pointing to it
    idat = make_idat(payload)

    # In iloc with construction_method = idat, offset is within the idat payload
    extent_offset = 0
    extent_length = len(payload)
    iloc = make_iloc(item_id, extent_offset, extent_length, use_large=False)

    # pitm: primary item box
    pitm = full_box(b"pitm", 0, 0, u16(item_id))

    # iprp: container for ipco and ipma
    iprp = box(b"iprp", ipco + ipma)

    # meta full box with children: hdlr, pitm, iinf, iloc, iprp, idat
    # hdlr: handler type: 'pict'
    hdlr_payload = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"pict" + b"\x00" * 12  # pre_defined, handler_type, reserved
    hdlr = full_box(b"hdlr", 0, 0, hdlr_payload)

    meta_children = hdlr + pitm + iinf + iloc + iprp + idat
    meta = full_box(b"meta", 0, 0, meta_children)
    return meta

# Make ftyp for avif or heic/heif

def make_ftyp(brand: str) -> bytes:
    if brand == "avif":
        major = b"avif"
        minor = 0
        comp = [b"avif", b"mif1", b"miaf", b"isom"]
    elif brand == "heic":
        major = b"heic"
        minor = 0
        comp = [b"heic", b"mif1", b"miaf", b"isom"]
    else:  # heif
        major = b"heif"
        minor = 0
        comp = [b"heif", b"mif1", b"miaf", b"isom"]

    payload = major + u32(minor) + b"".join(comp)
    return box(b"ftyp", payload)

# Choose minimal but plausible coded item types:
# - avif brand: item_type 'av01' (AV1 Image item)
# - heic/heif brand: item_type 'hvc1' (HEVC Image item)

def choose_item_type(brand: str) -> bytes:
    return b"av01" if brand == "avif" else b"hvc1"

# Generate minimal payload for item data. For container validity, any bytes are acceptable.
# Provide a few seeded patterns and sizes.

def make_payload(rng: random.Random, brand: str, bit_depth: int) -> bytes:
    # Small payload sizes are fine; stay under a few hundred bytes
    size = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256])
    if size == 0:
        return b""  # empty extent allowed with idat construction
    # Patterns
    patterns = []
    patterns.append(bytes([0] * size))
    patterns.append(bytes([255] * size))
    patterns.append(bytes((i * 37) & 0xFF for i in range(size)))
    patterns.append(rng.randbytes(size) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size)))
    return rng.choice(patterns)

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose brand and dimensions
    brand = rng.choice(["avif", "heic", "heif"]) 
    width = rng.choice([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128])
    height = rng.choice([1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128])
    bit_depth = rng.choice([8, 10, 12])
    add_rotation = rng.choice([True, False])
    add_mirror = rng.choice([True, False])

    ftyp = make_ftyp(brand)
    item_type = choose_item_type(brand)
    payload = make_payload(rng, brand, bit_depth)
    meta = make_meta(width, height, bit_depth, item_type, add_rotation, add_mirror, payload)

    # Final file: ftyp + meta
    data = ftyp + meta

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a small, valid baseline TIFF file (either 1-bit bilevel
# or 8-bit grayscale) with minimal tags. It supports little- or big-endian, and
# can vary image size, bits per sample, compression, and rows-per-strip layout.
# The output is a single bytes buffer suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME input.

# TIFF constants
TIFF_MAGIC_LE = b"II\x2A\x00"  # little-endian
TIFF_MAGIC_BE = b"MM\x00\x2A"  # big-endian

# Tag IDs
TAG_ImageWidth = 256
TAG_ImageLength = 257
TAG_BitsPerSample = 258
TAG_Compression = 259
TAG_Photometric = 262
TAG_StripOffsets = 273
TAG_SamplesPerPixel = 277
TAG_RowsPerStrip = 278
TAG_StripByteCounts = 279
TAG_PlanarConfig = 284
TAG_XResolution = 282
TAG_YResolution = 283
TAG_ResolutionUnit = 296

# TIFF types
TYPE_BYTE = 1
TYPE_ASCII = 2
TYPE_SHORT = 3
TYPE_LONG = 4
TYPE_RATIONAL = 5

# Compression
COMP_NONE = 1
COMP_LZW = 5  # We'll provide uncompressed by default; keep tag flexible.

# Photometric
PHOTO_WHITEISZERO = 0
PHOTO_BLACKISZERO = 1
PHOTO_RGB = 2
PHOTO_PALETTE = 3

# PlanarConfig
PLANAR_CONTIG = 1

# ResolutionUnit
RES_NONE = 1
RES_INCH = 2
RES_CENTIMETER = 3


def _pack_endian(endian: str, fmt: str, *vals: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(endian + fmt, *vals)


def _align_to(offset: int, align: int = 2) -> int:
    rem = offset % align
    return offset if rem == 0 else offset + (align - rem)


def _build_ifd_entry(endian: str, tag: int, ttype: int, count: int, value_or_offset: int) -> bytes:
    # IFD entry is: tag(2), type(2), count(4), value/offset(4)
    return _pack_endian(endian, 'HHII', tag, ttype, count, value_or_offset)


def _make_minimal_tiff(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose endianness
    be = rnd.choice([False, True])
    magic = TIFF_MAGIC_BE if be else TIFF_MAGIC_LE
    endian = '>' if be else '<'

    # Choose small dimensions
    width = rnd.choice([8, 16, 32, 64, 128])
    height = rnd.choice([8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64])

    # Choose bits per sample and photometric for grayscale
    # Prefer uncompressed for simplicity and libgd support
    bits_per_sample = rnd.choice([1, 8])  # 1-bit bilevel or 8-bit grayscale
    photometric = PHOTO_BLACKISZERO if bits_per_sample == 8 else rnd.choice([PHOTO_BLACKISZERO, PHOTO_WHITEISZERO])

    compression = COMP_NONE  # keep it simple and widely supported

    samples_per_pixel = 1
    planar_config = PLANAR_CONTIG

    # Basic strip layout: one strip or multiple
    rows_per_strip_choices = [height, max(1, height // 2), max(1, height // 4)]
    rows_per_strip = rnd.choice(rows_per_strip_choices)
    rows_per_strip = max(1, min(rows_per_strip, height))

    # Calculate image data size
    if bits_per_sample == 1:
        bytes_per_row = (width + 7) // 8
    else:
        bytes_per_row = width  # 8-bit grayscale
    image_bytes = bytes_per_row * height

    # Create simple pattern image data
    # Generate a few pattern variants to exercise decoding
    pattern_type = rnd.choice(['checker', 'vertical', 'horizontal', 'gradient'])
    buf = bytearray(image_bytes)
    if bits_per_sample == 1:
        # For bilevel, construct bit patterns
        for y in range(height):
            for xbyte in range(bytes_per_row):
                # Fill 8 pixels per byte
                byte = 0
                for b in range(8):
                    x = xbyte * 8 + b
                    if x >= width:
                        bit = 0
                    else:
                        if pattern_type == 'checker':
                            bit = ((x >> 1) ^ (y >> 1)) & 1
                        elif pattern_type == 'vertical':
                            bit = (x // 2) & 1
                        elif pattern_type == 'horizontal':
                            bit = (y // 2) & 1
                        else:  # gradient
                            bit = (x * 255 // max(1, width - 1)) > 127
                    byte |= (1 if bit else 0) << (7 - b)
                buf[y * bytes_per_row + xbyte] = byte
    else:
        # 8-bit grayscale
        for y in range(height):
            for x in range(width):
                if pattern_type == 'checker':
                    v = 255 if ((x // 4) ^ (y // 4)) & 1 else 0
                elif pattern_type == 'vertical':
                    v = 255 if (x // 3) & 1 else 32
                elif pattern_type == 'horizontal':
                    v = 255 if (y // 3) & 1 else 32
                else:  # gradient
                    v = (x * 255) // max(1, width - 1)
                buf[y * bytes_per_row + x] = v

    image_data = bytes(buf)

    # Strip partitioning
    num_strips = (height + rows_per_strip - 1) // rows_per_strip

    # Compute byte counts per strip (all contiguous for simplicity)
    strip_byte_counts: List[int] = []
    strip_offsets: List[int] = []

    # We will construct the file by laying out: header (8 bytes), IFD at some offset,
    # then data area containing arrays for tags and the image strips.

    # Start building: header + offset to first IFD (we will set offset later)
    # Reserve header 8 bytes: magic + ifd_offset
    file_bytes = bytearray()
    file_bytes += magic
    file_bytes += b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"  # placeholder for IFD offset

    # We'll assemble IFD entries and extra data in a scratch buffer to compute offsets
    ifd_entries: List[bytes] = []
    extra_data = bytearray()

    def add_value_or_offset(ttype: int, values: List[int], force_array: bool = False) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        # Returns (type, value_or_offset). Packs inline if fits 4 bytes; otherwise writes to extra_data and returns offset.
        count = len(values)
        # Helper to pack a list by type
        if ttype == TYPE_SHORT:
            packed = b"".join(_pack_endian(endian, 'H', v & 0xFFFF) for v in values)
        elif ttype == TYPE_LONG:
            packed = b"".join(_pack_endian(endian, 'I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF) for v in values)
        elif ttype == TYPE_BYTE:
            packed = bytes(v & 0xFF for v in values)
        elif ttype == TYPE_RATIONAL:
            # values are provided as pairs (num, den)
            packed = b"".join(_pack_endian(endian, 'II', values[i], values[i+1]) for i in range(0, len(values), 2))
        else:
            packed = b""
        # Inline if single SHORT or BYTE and 4 bytes or fewer and not forced array
        if not force_array and ((ttype == TYPE_SHORT and count == 1) or (ttype == TYPE_BYTE and count <= 4)):
            # Put packed into 4-byte field
            val = 0
            # For SHORT count=1, packed is 2 bytes; place in LSB of the 4-byte field respecting endianness
            if ttype == TYPE_SHORT:
                val = int.from_bytes(packed, byteorder='big' if be else 'little')
            elif ttype == TYPE_BYTE:
                val = int.from_bytes(packed.ljust(4, b"\x00"), byteorder='big' if be else 'little')
            return ttype, val
        # Otherwise, append to extra_data and return offset
        nonlocal_offset = 8  # header size
        # IFD will be placed after header; but extra_data begins after we know IFD size. We'll relocate later.
